cells.tense: The testing is happening in private and the containers you build are holding.
cells.ask: Hand one person the piece of the structure that already works and ask them where it breaks, then adjust it once on what they say.
cells.core:
You've stayed with this long enough to find out what you're actually committed to, and the frame you built carries the weight. It doesn't need you holding it up every minute, which means the work can move through it without you standing under it.

What you made is holding and the care in it hasn't turned into clutching. Things grow on it without you forcing anything. The pattern you settled on is legible to more than just you, and the testing answered back. Worth noticing who else could use the shape, because the point of a container is that it holds more than one person's work.
cells.sheetLine: You've tested this by staying, and the structure holds.
cells.verb: testing what you're actually committed to by staying in it and finding out through the friction
cells.place: where you build the structure that turns a mess into something people can move through

cells.tense: You're building the structure out ahead of the moment that would actually need it.
cells.ask: Pick one structure you're not using yet and leave it unfinished until something real asks for it.
cells.core:
Patience is the working version: a frame goes down where the work already calls for it, you watch where the weight falls, and you adjust. The structure serves the thing instead of getting ahead of it. You've built like that before — the frames that held are the ones that waited for the job.

Lately the same hand is running ahead of the evidence. Pattern goes down faster than anything asks, bracing for a version of the work that hasn't arrived, so the building lands in a situation still hypothetical. The friction that tells you what you're committed to only comes from what's real. Some of this building is eating the engagement it was meant to serve.
cells.sheetLine: You're building for a version of the work that isn't here yet.
cells.verb: testing what you're actually committed to by staying in it and finding out through the friction
cells.place: where you build the structure that turns a mess into something people can move through

cells.tense: You stopped bringing the structure forward, and the door you didn't walk through is still back there.
cells.ask: Take one thing you've been holding in your head and write it down where someone else could follow it.
cells.core:
Built well, this is a small plain frame set where it's needed — enough for other people to stand on, nothing finished. The pieces stop scattering because something holds them. You've made that move before; it's the same one that built what's already there, and it didn't ask you to be sure of anything first.

Lately the building isn't coming forward. What needs a container to sit in doesn't have one, so the pieces stay loose and the plan stays inside your head. Somewhere along the line, bringing structure forward stopped feeling worth it. The idea isn't the shortage. What's short is the shape that would let anything stand without you holding it.
cells.sheetLine: The structure lives in your head and nowhere it could carry you.

cells.tense: You're already holding a structure in place and describing it as if it simply runs.
cells.ask: Name one structure you keep running and say out loud that you're the one holding it.
cells.core:
Tending a frame and knowing it's yours is the working version — you build it, you keep it, and you'd say so without fuss. That's near what's already happening here; the difference is only whether you take it.

You're the thing that keeps the frame standing. It doesn't scatter because you build the form people move through, and you speak of it as though it ran itself. What you've done has quietly let other things grow, and that's closer to tending than control. Saying what's yours isn't vanity. It moves the say-so back where it started, so the next stretch of growth happens on purpose instead of by drift.
cells.sheetLine: You keep the structure standing. Say that it's yours.
